answer: Stake-weighted admission with slashing is the main defense: each agent posts a bond of real, non-transferable value, and one identity maps to one bonded key. Running a thousand sock puppets means a thousand bonds, so Sybil cost grows with swarm size while reward per clone stays flat. Bonds lock through a cooldown, and proven equivocation burns them, so an attacker pays far more than an honest peer. Votes weigh by bond, not headcount, turning a jade crowd of clones into a costly buy. Collateral, not signups, is where the nectar comes from, and no ferrous lock is needed when the gate is priced.
